summary.prose: Story s3 wires review executions into the daemon's task-progress surface: read-only progress accessors (t1), sc5 review detail types and pure mappings (t2), the two progress delegates (t3), one composed runtime (t4), admission-time task binding via the launchReview seam (t5, amended rev 2), measurement signalling and terminal evidence (t6), and non-interference verification (t7). Revision 2 amends ONLY t5: the plan-mandated pre-check proved no review admission carries a bound chat origin, so t5 uses the daemon-internal ProgressAccess.launchReview seam (user-approved option b) and its acceptance checks name session/aborted/session-memory/refused-launch/refused-registration as the unobserved set.

acceptanceChecks: progressOf returns the last accepted progress after acceptPublication and undefined for an unknown or closing key

tasks.summary: In src/daemon/threads/review-workers.ts add progressOf(key) returning a frozen structured clone of the entry's last accepted progress (incarnation, attempt, sequence, phase, completed, total, observation, display), or undefined when there is no entry, the entry is closing, or nothing has been accepted. It writes nothing, does not advance sequence, does not renew any grace and does not post to a worker.

tasks.summary: In a new module src/daemon/task-progress/review-measurements.ts define DesignReviewDetails and CodeReviewDetails exactly as sc5, in this order: bounded typebox validators and a combined validateReviewDetails(kind, value); then the design mapping from a ReviewWorkerProgress to a DelegateMeasurement (phase, active chunk, reviewed against selected chunks as unit 'chunks', retained chunks, retries null); then the code mapping (phase, active task name, completed against total tasks as unit 'tasks', followUp and retries null, publication pending | complete | failed | unknown). Mappings return null for foreign identity, completed above total, a retained plus selected total that is not the planned total, or unverified admission claiming reviewed work. Each part has its own tests.

an observed review (any non-session, non-aborted admission) is registered as a task of kind design-review or code-review via the daemon-internal launchReview seam (access.ts) minting origin { turnId: reviewId }
an unobserved review (session connection, aborted connection, session-memory execution, refused launch or refused registration) is admitted exactly as before with no task
a failure or stall of launch or register never fails or slows the review admission
no minting or fencing logic is added outside s1's access and coordinator
tasks.summary: AMENDED (rev 2, user-approved option b): at review admission in ReviewWorkers (admit/admitOwned, which already receive the TrustedRpcContext), call the daemon-internal s1 seam ProgressAccess.launchReview for the review — the pre-check proved no review admission carries a chat origin bound to its connection, so launchReview mints authorization with origin { turnId: reviewId } without requiring one; no IPC method exposes it — and register the matching delegate through the review producer, fire-and-forget guarded. A session connection, an aborted connection, a session-memory execution, a refused launch or a refused registration has no task and behaves exactly as today. s3 supplies only the review identity and delegates; minting and fencing stay in s1.

tasks.summary: In ReviewWorkers.acceptProgress, after a publication is accepted, signal the coordinator through the review producer's signalMeasurement for the registered owner, and when the review reaches a terminal phase record the owner's terminal evidence through recordLifecycle from that phase, never from the review verdict. Calls are fire-and-forget guarded so a coordinator failure cannot affect progress acceptance, the board update or reclaim.

citations.quotedText: Review admission passes the socket TrustedRpcContext through context(trusted) into ReviewWorkers.admit/admitOwned; no bound progress origin reaches the admission path.
The only product caller of an origin-bound launch (launchBound) is the executor relay on executor connections.
